text.p: VIENNA, July 28 (Reuter) The main stories in the Austrian press this Monday are:
DIE PRESSE
- Interior minister Karl Schloegl says he does not want to be without an army on Austria's eastern borders after 1999.
- The government faces a tricky situation over its 1998-1999 double budget: the opposition thinks reforms go too far, experts think they don't go far enough.
- Floods, rain and hail have caused damage of at least a few hundred million schillings to Austrian agriculture. More rain could mean crop failures.
- Sport article firm Kneissl Dachstein wants to list on foreign stock exchanges.
- OMV's supervisory board will consider plans to take over Czech Benzina and to extract natural gas in Algeria.
DER STANDARD
- SPOe party chairman Heinz Fischer says he would have nothing against the idea of a professional army so long as it were used in the defence of a neutral state.
- Some Austrian firms are profiting from the strong rise of the dollar and pound, according to Investment Bank Austria. Winners are OMV, Radex-Heraklith, Boehler-Uddeholm and Wienerberger.
- No Summer, no sun, no turnover: bad weather is not helping trade.
KURIER

- Conservative People's Party leader Wolfgang Schuessel, weakened by allegations over comments about foreign politicians and a recent poor performance in opinion polls, says he can take more than some people think.
- Food firm Mautner is to concentrate on mustard and vinegar in the east.
- Microsoft Austria heads towards its first billion schilling turnover, helped especially by development in the server market.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- President Thomas Klestil praised the government's double budget and pension reform.
- The Viennese family business Kwizda is to close all its chemist's shops in Austria.
- Defence minister Werner Fasslabend says that Austrian entry to NATO could yield economic benefits.
WIENER ZEITUNG
- The Institute for Higher Studies criticises planned pension reform, although changes to early retirement are welcomed.
